subject: Post-call: CloudScale procurement path & marketplace suitability
messages:

Subject: Post-call: CloudScale procurement path & marketplace suitability

Hi Daniel — thanks again for making time today. Quick recap from my side and a suggested set of next steps so your procurement team can evaluate options in parallel.

Call highlights (5 min):
- Use case: internal analytics platform (real-time alerting, embeddings for similarity) with ~10M monthly tokens, bursty traffic.
- SLA needs: <200ms p95 for inference on 512-token inputs, audit logs required.
- Procurement interest: curious about AWS Marketplace but need to compare PO (preferred by procurement) vs. corporate card for initial pilot.

Procurement options we discussed:
1) AWS Marketplace (Metered or AMI/contract) — fast procurement for cloud-native teams; can route billing to existing AWS account or use consolidated billing.
2) Direct purchase (invoice / PO) — Redwood Dedicated or Private; supports standard PO terms, custom SOW, and contract redlines.
3) Card (one-time) — simplest for POC but usually limited to smaller pilots.

Attached: a short SOW draft, an AWS marketplace quickstart guide, and an indicative quote for the pilot (worksheet).

Suggested next steps (we can run these in parallel):
- You: confirm which buying path procurement prefers (PO vs marketplace). If PO, we can send a template PO + standard terms.
- Procurement: if interested in AWS Marketplace, can they share the AWS Account ID and whether they need an AMI or metered SaaS contract?
- Redwood (Karthik/Marissa): provide final quote and timing, and call out any compliance items needed for SOC 2 evidence.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute procurement walkthrough with Karthik next week. Available slots: Tue/Wed 9–11am PT.

Thanks — Jasmine

--

Thanks Jasmine — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement preference: our purchasing team prefers PO for anything >$10k ARR. For pilots we can sometimes use a corporate card but need budget owner sign-off.
- Marketplace interest: we like the idea of Marketplace for faster deployment, but billing via our AWS account needs approval from cloud ops (they control AMI/roles).
- Compliance ask: procurement will want to see SOC 2 Type II dates and an export of retention/audit log policies.

I'll loop in procurement (procurement@cloudscale.com) and cloud-ops next. Can Karthik send the formal PO template and the SOC 2 pointer? Also, what's the minimum commitment for a pilot on Dedicated vs Marketplace?

Best,
Daniel Ortega

Hi all — quick answers to procurement questions and a note on tradeoffs.

1) PO vs. Marketplace (practical differences)
- AWS Marketplace (SaaS metered): Pros = faster procurement for cloud-native buyers, rolling metered billing, simple signup; Cons = requires AWS account mapping and sometimes causes delays for enterprise legal to accept marketplace terms.
- PO (invoice): Pros = standard for enterprise procurement, supports custom SOW and SLA addenda; Cons = longer lead time (typically 1–3 weeks for standard PO from signature to first invoice).

2) Minimum commitments:
- Marketplace metered pilot: no formal minimum, 30-day trial workable but typical pilots run 30–90 days at expected usage.
- Dedicated/Private: we usually recommend a 3–6 month pilot commitment to justify reserved capacity; can do 30-day pilot on shared capacity with a POC pricing sheet (we attached an indicative quote).

3) Compliance evidence: attaching the public SOC 2 page link and I can provide a redacted audit summary on request. For retention/audit logs, we support exportable audit logs and can sign reasonable access clauses in the SOW.

4) Next actions I can take:
- Share PO template (I'll drop in the doc link).
- Confirm what we can include in the SOW for SLA and audit access.
- Set up a 30-minute procurement session with procurement@cloudscale.com.

Marissa, can you prepare the quote worksheet for the Dedicated pilot option with both card and PO line items?

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
